can_do_statement: Can use 'much' with uncountable nouns in negative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Quantifying uncountable entities in absence or low quantity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'not much' to describe a small amount of something you can't count.

positives: We didn't have much money for the trip.
I haven't got much time to watch television.
negatives: We had much money for the trip.
She hasn't seen many friends lately.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of quantifying determiners with singular nouns ('a', 'every').► determiners: articles

ontology.mental_model: Singling out a specific countable entity or referring to all instances distributively.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'a' for one thing or 'every' for all things of that type.

positives: I go to college every day.
I have a big kitchen in my house.
negatives: I go to college all days.
I have big kitchens in my house.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with singular nouns ('each', 'an', 'one' and numbers).

ontology.mental_model: Specifying exact quantities or individual components of a group.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'each', 'an', 'one', or numbers to talk about single items.

positives: Each class is about one hour long.
We have an extra ticket for the concert.
negatives: All classes are long.
We have some extra tickets.

guideword: FORM: WITH PLURAL AND UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use a range of quantifying determiners ('some', 'any', 'no', 'more', 'a lot of') with both plural nouns and uncountable nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing indefinite quantities for both countable and uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'some', 'any', 'no', 'more', 'a lot of' for things you have many of, or can't count.

positives: I think we should bring some water.
There were no clouds in the sky.
negatives: I think we should bring a bottle.
There was not a cloud.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with plural nouns ('all', 'both', 'a few').

ontology.mental_model: Quantifying plural entities as totalities or small subsets.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'all', 'both', or 'a few' to talk about multiple things.

positives: This notice is for all students.
I'm just writing to tell you a few things.
negatives: This notice is for every student.
I'm just writing to tell you one thing.

can_do_statement: Can use 'many' with plural nouns in negative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing absence of a large quantity for countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'not many' to say there are only a few of something.

positives: There aren't many tickets left.
I haven't got many winter clothes.
negatives: There are many tickets.
I haven't got much time.

can_do_statement: Can use 'so many' and 'too many' with plural nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing an excessively or surprisingly large quantity of countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so many' or 'too many' to exaggerate a lot of things.

positives: We played so many games together.
I know I bought too many things.
negatives: We played many games.
I know I bought too much food.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners + 'of' + determiner ('half of', 'enough of', 'none of',).► pronouns

ontology.mental_model: Specifying a proportion of a definite subset.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'half of', 'enough of', or 'none of' followed by 'the' or 'my'.

positives: You should spend half of your holiday with parents.
None of the stores had it.
negatives: You should spend half a holiday.
No stores had it.

guideword: FORM: WITH PLURAL AND UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of quantifying determiners with both plural nouns and uncountable nouns ('most', 'enough', 'plenty of', 'loads of').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing sufficiency, majority, or abundance for countable and uncountable entities.

positives: I am convinced that most people watch TV.
We will have plenty of time to buy tickets.
negatives: I am convinced that many people watch TV.
We will have a lot of time to buy tickets.

guideword: FORM: 'SO MUCH', 'TOO MUCH' WITH UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
can_do_statement: Can use 'so much' and 'too much' with uncountable nouns.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing an excessively or surprisingly large quantity of uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so much' or 'too much' to exaggerate a lot of something.

positives: I have so much work at the moment.
My neighbours are making too much noise.
negatives: I have a lot of work.
My neighbours are making too many noises.

can_do_statement: Can use 'much' with uncountable nouns in interrogative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about the quantity of uncountable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking questions using 'much' with uncountable things.

positives: How much television do you watch?
Do you have much time left?
negatives: I don't watch much television.
How many televisions do you have?

can_do_statement: Can use quantifying determiners with uncountable nouns, often in informal and/or spoken contexts ('a little', 'a bit of' and 'a little bit of').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing a small, indefinite quantity of uncountable entities in informal contexts.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'a little', 'a bit of', or 'a little bit of'.

positives: We could spend a little time together.
I just watch a little bit of TV.
negatives: We could spend some time together.
I watch a lot of TV.

can_do_statement: Can use 'many' with plural nouns in interrogative contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about the quantity of countable entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Asking questions using 'many' with plural things.

positives: Have you got many friends in England?
How many channels are there in Britain?
negatives: I don't have many friends.
How much money do you have?

can_do_statement: Can use a range of quantifying determiners + 'of' + determiner ('all of', 'some of', 'both of', 'many of', 'any of', number + 'of', 'each of'). ► pronouns: quantity

ontology.mental_model: Specifying a proportion of a definite subset.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'all of', 'some of', 'both of', 'many of', 'any of', or numbers with 'of the' or 'of my'.

positives: I spent all of my money!
Some of my friends gave me books.
negatives: I spent all my money!
Some friends gave me books.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of quantifying determiners with plural nouns ('several', 'millions of', 'a few of').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing larger or diverse quantities of countable entities.

positives: Several days ago we received a complaint.
They interviewed a few of the students.
negatives: Many days ago we received a complaint.
They interviewed some students.
